QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_42

question.text: A Focus Group Discussion (FGD) with 8-10 beneficiaries is MOST appropriate for the SIA when:

answer.text: Exploring mechanisms, unexpected outcomes, and community-level dynamics that survey instruments cannot easily capture
Computing a statistically representative point estimate of coverage
Issuing a reasonable-assurance opinion on monetised SROI outcome value
Replacing the need for quantitative baseline data

explanation.text: The Logic: FGDs are qualitative tools designed to surface mechanisms, unexpected effects, community norms and narrative context. They are NOT a substitute for quantitative sampling when you need a statistically representative point estimate or a defensible SROI number — they complement quantitative evidence. The Trap: Options B, C, D all misuse FGDs. Point estimates require random samples. Assurance needs documented evidence procedures. Quantitative baselines cannot be replaced by group chat. Cross-Exam Context: Research-methodology syllabi across X-A IA and XV use FGDs similarly. XXIII applies to SIA triangulation under SAS-100. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Record and transcribe FGDs with beneficiary consent — the audit trail (audio + transcript) is what distinguishes an SIA-grade FGD from an NGO focus group used for internal planning only.
